original_question: For any configuration of N fixed electric charges in R^3 that has only finitely many equilibrium points, is the number of equilibrium points always at most (N - 1)^2?
target_in_paper: Boris Shapiro, Section 2 "On Maxwell’s problem", Conjecture 2 (J. C. Maxwell) in arXiv:2312.07754; for the precise point-charge/potential setup, this restates the classical formulation cited there from [GNSh], Section 1, Conjecture 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core statement very well: it asks about an arbitrary configuration of N fixed charges in R^3, assumes the set of equilibrium points is finite, and uses the exact quadratic upper bound (N - 1)^2 that Maxwell’s conjecture asserts.
missing_details: The objects are point charges, not general charge distributions.
The equilibrium points are points of the electrostatic field, equivalently critical points of the electrostatic potential, away from the charge locations.
To make the question stand-alone, the potential should be written explicitly as V(x) = sum_{i=1}^N q_i / |x - x_i| on R^3 \ {x_1, ..., x_N}.
The charges should be identified as fixed nonzero real values q_1, ..., q_N at fixed distinct points x_1, ..., x_N in R^3.
The Maxwell statement in this section has no positivity restriction on the charges; the neighboring finiteness conjecture for positive charges is a different conjecture.

In the original source [GNSh] cited by the paper, the classical version is phrased for configurations whose equilibrium points are all nondegenerate; that stronger hypothesis is sufficient for finiteness but is not identical to the survey’s phrasing.
refined_question: Let x_1, ..., x_N be distinct fixed points in R^3 carrying nonzero real point charges q_1, ..., q_N, and let V(x) = sum_{i=1}^N q_i / |x - x_i| for x in R^3 \ {x_1, ..., x_N}. Suppose the electrostatic field ∇V has only finitely many zeros in R^3 \ {x_1, ..., x_N} (equivalently, V has only finitely many critical points). Is the total number of such equilibrium points always at most (N - 1)^2?
justification: The draft matches almost verbatim the Maxwell-type open problem recorded by Shapiro in arXiv:2312.07754: Conjecture 2 asks whether any configuration of fixed electric charges in R^3 with finitely many equilibrium points has at most (N - 1)^2 such points. The nearby Remark 2 explains that the finiteness hypothesis is generic. To make the question mathematically self-contained, I made explicit the standard Coulomb potential, the fact that the equilibria are zeros of the electric field / critical points of the potential, and that the charges are point charges with fixed locations and real values. I did not replace the question by the neighboring positive-charge finiteness conjecture (Conjecture 3 in the same section) or by the stronger Voronoi-diagram conjectures from [GNSh], because those are related but different problems.

citations.label: Equation (1.1) and surrounding definition of critical points as equilibrium points
